changes.summary: The Musée d’Orsay is celebrating its 40th birthday with a rotation of major new acquisitions that reflect the diversity of its collections. The exceptional dation of the Portrait de l’artiste by Gustave Caillebotte (1848-1894), which the Museum has just received, opens the series, which will continue throughout 2026. It’s Gustave Caillebotte’s most important self-portrait. It was painted and exhibited in 1879, when the 31-year-old artist was on the way to becoming a major figure in the impressionist movement. He depicts himself at work in his studio, observing himself in a mirror and painting the portrait we’re looking at. His studio was also a place for socializing and presenting his personal collection of paintings. The artist supported his impressionist friends by purchasing their works, which he went on to bequeath to the State at his death. Renoir’s Bal du moulin de la Galette [Dance at the Moulin de la Galette] is hanging on the wall. This self-portrait dialogues with another of Caillebotte’s self-portraits from the Musée d’Orsay’s collections, painted a few months before the artist’s untimely death at the age of 45. The Musée d’Orsay has seen a numerous remarkable additions to its collection of Caillebotte’s works since 2019, with Marie-Jeanne Daurelle’s bequest, three dations and the purchase of a national treasure. The Musée d’Orsay currently conserves 16 of the artist’s works.
